genericProblem: An owner-command seed can authenticate a role but still fail every project-scoped command when it treats login as a project selection, omits the owner-issued context-version transition, or sends a retired client project field. Diagnostic sanitization can simultaneously hide the stage that identifies the broken boundary.
finiteDenominator: formal executor session entry and select-data-node operations
formal executor store create and status transitions
formal executor contract create and invalidation
store and contract closed request bodies
counterexamples: GROUP-scoped writes and project creation do not require a selected PROJECT.
Operations project-user invitation commands are not called by the formal executor and are not expanded into this repair.
A sensitive raw failure message must be redacted even when a controlled stage ID is retained.

findings.evidence: The failed run completed login and all prerequisite owner commands, then received 403 on its first store create. The executor did not call selectOperationsWorkspaceSessionDataNode, while controllers resolve the owner-confirmed selected project.
findings.minimumFix: Read session context after login, select only on project transitions with rolling owner contextVersion, and cover every current project-scoped command.

findings.evidence: seed-report safeFailure strips lower-case and hyphen characters, collapsing store-store-operating to --.
findings.minimumFix: Retain a controlled symbolic stage vocabulary while redacting all secret-bearing value shapes.
